what: The report-shape node claimed two findings about different paths cannot share one help entry. The command dedupes on the repair text, and five of nine bridge repairs plus all four instruction repairs ignore the path argument, so they do collapse. Corrected to state the dedupe rule as implemented.

Three nodes claimed every bridge finding repairs through the init skill. Three of the nine name no skill at all: two reconcile by hand because rebuilding discards the newer edit, and one corrects the git index. All three nodes and the seam node now agree with the guidance table.

The seam between the two renderings of each repair was unowned: one names a shell invocation for the command, the other names a skill for the shipped skill, and only the second names an owner. Stated in the seam node with a scenario pinning both.

A settings-entry instruction bridge reports ok whether or not the file it names exists, so it can be ok in the same run that reports no-instructions. Correct as shipped, previously unspecified and untested; now both.

Round-one judge raised a grammar slip in a scenario title that a commit in this same round had introduced. By provenance that is a regression rather than a fresh finding, and doctrine stops the loop for a re-plan. Judged not to apply: the class doctrine targets is a substantive finding recurring on ground a round claimed to have fixed, and this is an incomplete sentence left by an otherwise correct edit, with no bearing on any contract. Recorded rather than silently absorbed.

Round one recorded the bridge-ownership rule as applied everywhere. It had been applied to the instances already read rather than swept for, and a fourth survived in a different section of one of the same files. The remediation rule is to state the rule and sweep for its other instances; I did the first and not the second. Swept by grep this round.

The report-shape node described a deduplication branch the shipped table cannot reach: since the repair split, every repair arising at more than one path names that path, and the two that do not are reported once per repository. Restated as a guard rather than a behavior, and its scenario rebuilt to render the real table at two paths rather than to assert against fabricated findings.

One gate finding was not a defect: a blank line said to split a scenario map into two tables had already been closed in an earlier round, and the judge reported it against a state that no longer existed. Reported back rather than actioned.
